title: Restricted Mean Survival Effects from Combined Incident and Prevalent Cohorts
banked_reason: D-0.5 NO-PASS after seven REVISE reviews: proposal failed to converge within two bounded root revisions; final review flags notation coherence and the omitted LumleyShawDai2011 calibration comparator.
gap_reasons: The declared symbol is \(\mathcal T_n\), while the construction and lower-bound display use \(\mathfrak T_n\); similarly \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcalEta\) are used interchangeably, so the action and primitive-law spaces need one consistent notation.

The survey omits the closest generic comparator, LumleyShawDai2011, which explicitly connects known-margin survey calibration to semiparametric incomplete-data estimators and precision gains; the draft must distinguish its standard projection mechanism from the claimed singular delayed-entry contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: Seven D-0.5 proposal versions attempted to specify and position a known-margin triangular RMST efficiency frontier. The final review no longer flagged the onset-scale process definitions or proposed coefficient, but still returned REVISE for inconsistent notation and an omitted calibration comparator; the bounded review budget ended before any D0 derivation or Lean proof. The mathematical kernel remains unrefuted and is marked retry, not established.
tldr: A naturally recruited incident cohort of size \(n/\log n\) contributes the early failures that regularize a stationary prevalent cohort of size \(n\), producing causal restricted-mean risk of order \(\log\log n/n\). On the common onset-time scale, the observed prevalent exit \(W_P=U+Y_P\) yields the predictable risk indicator \(\mathbf 1\{U<t\le W_P\}\) and the censoring-sensitive kernel \(K_P(t)=\int_0^tG_P(t-u\mid u)\,du\). Exact population stratum margins constrain the resulting slow endpoint score even though treatment propensities are unknown. With \(D(P_n)\) defined by the exact normalized risk-set integral, the coefficient sequence is \(C_N(P_n)=w^{\mathsf T}[D-DL^{\mathsf T}(LDL^{\mathsf T})^{-1}LD]w\), its gain over the free-cell benchmark is a weighted across-stratum variance, and a feasible stopped product-limit estimator attains it by calibrating with observed entries before \(\tau\). The formal contribution is a full-experiment local minimax lower bound over all measurable two-sample actions, a uniform mean-square expansion, and projected tied-failure Greenwood studentization.
gap: Fixed-design biased-sampling NPMLE efficiency theory, fixed-mixture combined-cohort product-limit asymptotics, abstract-level combined-NPMLE asymptotic properties, fixed-regime propensity-score-adjusted Cox treatment-effect inference, and fixed-law counterfactual-survival inference do not determine the sharp risk of causal RMST when the incident share is \(1/\log n\). Existing covariate-distribution arguments establish that prevalent frequencies can contain information, but they neither profile unknown propensities at the singular endpoint scale nor exploit exact population margins through an observable nonparametric RMST calibration.
fill: The project derives the constrained coefficient from explicit failure and left-predictable risk processes on the lifetime-onset scale, fixes a non-indexed primitive base law \(\eta_0\), and induces \(P_{0,n}=\Gamma_{\rho_n}(\eta_0)\). The prevalent process yields \(K_{P,ax}(t)=\int_0^tG_P(t-u\mid a,x,u)\,du\), and its exact normalized risk-set integral defines \(D(P_n)\) and \(\Sigma_\psi(P_n)=\operatorname{diag}(\psi)D(P_n)\operatorname{diag}(\psi)\) without adding censoring regularity at entry. The observed-entry derivative yields the stated projection. The lower bound ranges over all measurable maps of both samples and exact \(p\) after profiling unknown propensity directions. A predictable stopping argument must prove uniform \(L^2\) and fourth-moment remainders with random multinomial cell counts, after which the exact tied-failure projected Greenwood sum is feasible without estimating tail means or endpoint densities.
